title: Abel identification and algebraic group law on a pointed genus-one curve
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $Y/k$ be a smooth projective connected curve [def-sc-curves, def-kun-projective] of genus $g(Y)=1$ [def-sc-genus], and let $O\in Y(k)$. Write $\operatorname{Pic}^0(Y)$ for the group of degree-zero invertible sheaf classes [def-sc-pic0, def-sc-invertible-module], with addition induced by tensor product, and $\mathcal O_Y(P-O)$ for the divisor line bundle [def-sc-divisor, lem-sc-divisor-class-curve]. There exist $k$-morphisms $m:Y\times_kY\to Y$ and $\iota:Y\to Y$ which make $Y$ a commutative group scheme with identity $O$. For this group law the map $\alpha_O:Y(k)\to\operatorname{Pic}^0(Y)$ given by $P\mapsto[\mathcal O_Y(P-O)]$ is a bijective group homomorphism. This is the elliptic group law associated with the origin $O$; in particular $\alpha_O(P+Q)=\alpha_O(P)+\alpha_O(Q)$ and $\alpha_O(O)=0$.

source.place: Tag 0DSV, example-pos-dim, genus-one paragraph: the degree-one Abel map is an isomorphism and identifying Picard degree one with degree zero gives the abelian-variety structure.

proof.text: The given smooth connected curve is integral by [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings]. It is projective by hypothesis and proper by [lem-pc-projective-proper]. With the given point $O$, [prop-pc-xk-integral] makes it geometrically integral. The genus conventions agree by [lem-pc-genus-agrees-sc], so its Picard-chapter genus is $1$. For the current blueprint's relative-dimension formulation, [lem-sc-curve-base-change-relative-dimension-one] with $T=\operatorname{Spec}k$ supplies smooth relative dimension $1$. The field is separably closed because it is algebraically closed. Thus [thm-sc-jacobian-representability] supplies a Jacobian $(J,\varphi)$, with $\varphi:\operatorname{Pic}^0_{Y/k}\simeq h_J$ an isomorphism of group-valued functors and $\varphi_k:\operatorname{Pic}^0(Y)\simeq J(k)$.

source.place: Tags 0B9Z (proposition-pic-curve) and 0BA0 (lemma-picard-pieces); Milne III Theorem 1.6, printed p.88

proof.text: Let $H_1$ represent $\operatorname{Hilb}^1_{Y/k}$, using [thm-pc-hilb-curves]. Its $T$-points are the closed subschemes $D\subset Y\times_kT$ finite locally free of degree one over $T$ [def-pc-hilb-functor]. By [lem-pc-flf-properties], $q_*\mathcal O_D$ is a locally free rank-one algebra. Locally write it as $Rb$, with $1=ub$ and $b^2=vb$; then $b=1b=uvb$, hence $uv=1$. Thus the unit $R\to Rb$ is an isomorphism, and $q:D\to T$ is an isomorphism. Consequently $D$ is the graph of a unique $T\to Y$. Conversely, $Y\times_kT\to T$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], hence separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]; the graph is a section and is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion]. It is isomorphic to $T$, hence finite locally free of degree one. The constructions are inverse and commute with every base change, including nonreduced $T$. Therefore $H_1\simeq Y$ by [lem-pc-representable-unique].

source.place: Tag 0B94 (Hilbert functor) and Tag 0B9I (proposition-hilb-d), degree one; rank-one algebra calculation written here

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-symmetric-abel-image-geometry] with $C=Y$, $P=O$, and $g=1$. It gives the closed immersion $e=f_O:Y\to J$. Under Step 2, its degree-one Abel morphism $f_O^{(1)}:H_1\to J$ is $e$: both associate to the universal graph divisor its divisor line bundle, then tensor with $\mathcal O_Y(-O)$ and apply the same representing isomorphism $\varphi$. The universal-divisor characterization in [lem-sc-hilb-to-pic-morphism] makes this an equality of morphisms, not merely of maps on $k$-points. The same general Abel-image theorem states $W_g=J$, so $g=1$ says that the scheme-theoretic image of $e$ is $J$. By [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image] its kernel ideal is zero. Since $e$ is a closed immersion, locally it is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], with $I$ this kernel. Hence $I=0$ on every affine open, so $e$ is an isomorphism of $k$-schemes. Its value at $O$ is $\varphi_k([\mathcal O_Y(O-O)])=0$.

source.place: III Proposition 2.3, printed pp.92–93, and Theorem 5.1(a), printed p.101; the genus-one consequence agrees with Stacks Tag 0DSV (moduli-curves.tex, example-pos-dim)

proof.text: Write $m_J$ and $\iota_J$ for the group operations of $J$ [def-sc-jacobian, def-sc-abelian-variety]. Define $m=e^{-1}\circ m_J\circ(e\times e)$ and $\iota=e^{-1}\circ\iota_J\circ e$, which are $k$-morphisms. For every $k$-scheme $T$, these operations on $Y(T)$ are exactly those of $J(T)$ under the bijection $e_T$. Associativity, both unit identities and both inverse identities therefore follow by cancelling $e_T$. The group $J(T)$ is commutative because $\varphi_T$ identifies it with the abelian group $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{Y/k}(T)$ [def-sc-picard-functor, def-sc-jacobian]. Thus commutativity also holds on $Y(T)$; by [lem-pc-yoneda] these are identities of scheme morphisms. Since $e(O)=0$, the identity section is $O$. This constructs the elliptic group law with the specified origin.

source.place: Tag 0DSV (example-pos-dim), genus-one paragraph: transferring the Picard group scheme structure; explicit conjugation formulas written here

proof.text: On $k$-points the Abel formula is $e_k(P)=\varphi_k([\mathcal O_Y(P-O)])$. Thus $\alpha_O=\varphi_k^{-1}\circ e_k$. Both factors are bijections, and each is a group homomorphism: $e_k$ by the definition of $m$ in Step 4, and $\varphi_k^{-1}$ by [thm-sc-jacobian-representability]. The target group here is exactly the kernel of the degree map [def-sc-pic0], whose addition is tensor product of invertible sheaf classes. Therefore $\alpha_O$ is the required bijective group homomorphism, $\alpha_O(P+Q)=\alpha_O(P)+\alpha_O(Q)$, and $\alpha_O(O)=[\mathcal O_Y]=0$.

Step 1: integrality (sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings), H-projective plus quasi-compact gives def-pc-projective-morphism, proper (pc-projective-proper), geometrically integral (prop-pc-xk-integral, algebraically closed implies separably closed, rational point O), genus agreement, then thm-sc-jacobian-representability. Step 2: Hilb^1 is identified with Y via the rank-one calculation (1=ub, b^2=vb, so uv=1, so q is an isomorphism), graph sections closed through proper base change and the section lemma, then representable-unique. It holds over nonreduced T and T empty. Step 3: symmetric-abel-image-geometry with g=1 (allowed by g>=1) gives f_O as a closed immersion and W_1=J. f^(1) composed with the Hilb^1 identification equals f_O, by the universal graph divisor and lem-sc-hilb-to-pic-morphism, and also by reducedness of Y. Since a closed immersion is quasi-compact, the kernel ideal is I=0, so e is an isomorphism. Steps 4 and 5: the group law is transported by conjugation, commutativity comes from Pic^0 being Ab-valued plus Yoneda, identity O since e(O)=0, and alpha_O=phi_k^{-1}∘e_k is a group bijection. Characteristics 2 and 3 cause no issue; genus 0 is excluded. This matches Milne's route, which is equivalent to the Stacks 0DSV route.
